mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.00% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher borrowing costs depressing equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from a pre-trigger period (p > 0.05), or the Fed holds rates below 5.00% within the next 30 days, reversing the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% simultaneously predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 AND UNRATE < 4.0 in the same month
failure_condition: In regimes where inflation is above 3%, the forward return is negative or non-significant (p > 0.10), or the employment/unemployment pattern reverses direction within the next 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average while consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 5.0 triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as it signals supply-side expansion without price pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 12-month MA AND CPIAUCSL < 5.0 in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or indistinguishable from a neutral period (no out-of-sample improvement), or CPIAUCSL spikes above 5.0 within 10 days, negating the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 5% for three consecutive months, without a concurrent drop in industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as weak consumer demand outweighs supply resilience.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥5% for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO does not fall by ≥5% in the same window
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive or statistically insignificant (p > 0.10), or industrial production also declines by ≥5% within the next 30 days, reversing the pattern.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 2.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be negative due to a tightening policy response to a labor market recovery.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 AND FEDFUNDS > 2.5 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market recovery with policy tightening
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive or statistically significant (p < 0.05), or the Fed cuts rates within 30 days, invalidating the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs for four consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it reflects robust labor market absorption and corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.10), or the increase in PAYEMS reverses direction within the next 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) measured by a 2% drop in the CPIAUCSL index in a single month, while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for two months, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as it signals deflationary pressure easing supply costs.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops by ≥2.0 in one month AND INDPRO is flat for the following two months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or indistinguishable from a neutral period, or CPIAUCSL recovers by ≥2.0 within the next 10 days, reversing the signal.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.50% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days is expected to be positive as lower policy rates reduce discounting of future cash flows and encourage risk-taking.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative or not statistically significant (p > 0.10), or FEDFUNDS rises above 1.50 within 30 days, ending the easing regime.
